sample.question:
Gear Train is a mechanical reasoning puzzle. Several spur gears are mounted on a fixed panel; gears never move sideways, they can only spin in place. Two gears are meshed if and only if their toothed rims touch in the image. Each gear is labeled with a letter and its number of teeth is printed under the letter (for example '12T' means 12 teeth). Meshed gears obey two laws: (1) they always spin in opposite directions, and (2) they pass the same number of teeth per unit time, so teeth_A x turns_A = teeth_B x turns_B. The driver gear is marked with a red circular arrow showing its spin direction. A chain of meshed gears forming a closed loop with an ODD number of gears cannot spin at all - the whole train jams.

In this panel some gears form a closed loop. The driver gear D tries to spin counterclockwise. What happens?

Options:
[1] The train spins freely and gear E turns clockwise
[2] The train spins freely and gear E turns counterclockwise
[3] The whole train is jammed - no gear can spin
sample.analysis:
All meshing pairs are: A-B, A-D, B-C, B-E, C-D.
Gears A-D-C-B form a closed loop of 4 gears - an EVEN number, so directions alternate consistently around the loop and nothing jams; the train can spin.
Path from the driver to gear E: D -> C -> B -> E.
Gear D spins counterclockwise, so its meshed neighbor gear C spins clockwise.
Gear C spins clockwise, so its meshed neighbor gear B spins counterclockwise.
Gear B spins counterclockwise, so its meshed neighbor gear E spins clockwise.
So the answer is: the train spins and gear E turns clockwise. The option number is 1.
options: The train spins freely and gear E turns clockwise
The train spins freely and gear E turns counterclockwise
The whole train is jammed - no gear can spin

state_content.rules: meshed gears spin in opposite directions; teeth x turns is equal for meshed gears; an odd loop jams
